data.title: Flash sessions: --flash PROFILE at creation, the unlock-cycle hint, and flash in sav
data.description:
Why: the flash-chip model (gbcli-flash, e9cba4f) is reachable only from Rust (CoreConfig::flash). An agent building a GB Studio batteryless game, or any flash-save cart, cannot model its save from the CLI or protocol.

RULINGS (Ben, 2026-11-07; recorded in project/2026-11-07-flash-model.md, "Decided"):
- `--flash PROFILE` at session creation, like --model/--seed: named profiles only (no parameter overrides), stored in the bundle meta and as an optional checkpoint-header field (the profile name), checked on restore like the model (a conflict is bad_request), kept by power-cycle.
- A hint on sessions without a board: when a run sees a write that is an unlock cycle for some board, warn and name the flag with a matching profile.
- On a flash session, `sav` and `power-cycle --sav` export and import the flash save area as well as SRAM.
- Flash notes surface on the run that took them as warning rows and --json fields.
- The server's rebuild path (power_cycle across a rebuilt ROM) carries the flash contents as it carries the battery.

Wait for the independent review of e9cba4f (FFI, unsafe, blob format 4) before building on it; fix its findings first.

criteria.label: a session created with --flash runs, checkpoints, restores and power-cycles on that board (tests)
restore across boards is bad_request; a mask-ROM session that sends unlock cycles warns with the flag
sav and power-cycle --sav carry the flash save area on a flash session
help, schema and design doc document the flag

data.title: Flash review fixes: mapper chosen from the padded size, command-address mask, notes lost on a refused load
data.description:
Findings from the review of e9cba4f, each with its probe in L00RuF-review_probes_flash.rs (run: cargo test -p gbcli-sameboy --test review_probes_flash -- --nocapture; four fail on purpose).

1. Low-medium. Padding the ROM to the chip size changes which mapper SameBoy picks. crates/sameboy/src/lib.rs:69-87 pads before GB_load_rom_from_buffer, and GB_configure_cart (crates/sameboy-sys/SameBoy/Core/mbc.c:190, :262) reads the padded size: (a) an MBC3 image on a board over 2 MiB (mx29lv320et, 4 MiB) becomes MBC30, widening the bank register to 8 bits (probe_mbc3_on_a_4mib_board_becomes_mbc30: "$2000<-$81: mask-ROM bank 1, flash bank 129"); (b) a ROM-only image ($0147=$00) padded past 32 KiB is treated as MBC3 (probe_rom_only_on_a_board_gains_an_mbc). The mapper type must come from the image's header, as on a mask-ROM session; only reach must grow.

2. Low; hardware half SUSPECTED. profiles.rs:166 sets command_mask 0x7FFF and profile.rs:133 compares bank*$4000+offset under it, so $4AAA/$4555 unlock cycles in the $4000 window match only on banks of one parity (probe_unlock_in_the_4000_window_depends_on_bank_parity: [(1,false,1),(2,true,0),(3,false,1),(4,true,0)] on generic-wr-aaa-aa). The reviewer recalls AMD 29LV160-class datasheets treating A11 and up as don't-care for command cycles; SST39SF040 decodes 15 bits. Check the datasheets (cite them) and set each profile's mask from its chip family.

3. Low. A load SameBoy refuses drops the chip's pending notes: the flash section loads first (lib.rs:648), FlashChip::load calls take_notes (state.rs:60), and the rollback at lib.rs:653 restores array and mode but not the notes (probe_a_refused_load_drops_pending_notes). A refused load must leave the core exactly as it was.

criteria.label: an MBC3 image on a 4 MiB board and a ROM-only image on any board keep their header's mapper (tests from the probes)
each profile's command-address mask is sourced from its chip's datasheet, and the 4000-window probe passes or is documented
a refused load leaves pending notes in place (test)

data.title: Project-level shared_shade lists colors an image's own warning already names together
data.description:
Found by the independent review of d0e891a (GTXXyr), 2026-11-07, by trace (the reviewer's shell had no cargo; probe not run).

Low. crates/build/src/images/shared.rs:181-189: a color counts as "apart" when it is apart from ANY other color in its shade, and then every apart color is listed. Repro: cave.png holds #000000 and #101010, bug.png holds #202020, all nearest to shade 3. cave.png gets its own shared_shade; the project-level shared_shade lists all three (count=3) and says "they are in different images, so no image's own shared_shade warning names them together", which is false for the #000000/#101010 pair. Images named are right; no shade changes. Fix: list only the colors with no image in common with some other listed color, or reword the message and count to say which pairs are apart.

Also found (finding 1, low): palette.rs:93-105 accepts `#ffffff #aaaaaa` on one line and drops the second color, because the rest only has to start with '#'. Not filed here: assets/palette.txt is replaced by assets/palettes.txt in the GBC plan (leaf palettes), which carries it as a criterion.

criteria.label: the cave/bug repro lists only colors no image's warning names together, with a true message and count (test)

data.description:
Why: everything after this needs a target flag to hang on. What: a --gbc flag on `gbcli build` (crates/build, wired in crates/cli). rgbfix gets -c, and the build result records the target. Without the flag nothing changes: today's call is `rgbfix -v -p 0xFF` at crates/build/src/project.rs:263.

data.title: Derived DMG version, and the .dmg.png override (color art)
data.description:
Why: dual mode needs a 4-shade version of every color image. What:
- Under --gbc, the DMG version is derived from the color image: each color takes its nearest DMG shade by lightness. This is Ben's rule from leaf ygc9bb; reuse its code in crates/build/src/images/shades.rs.
- ygc9bb's shared-shade warning is scoped to colors within one tile or object (plan question 2), with the remedy naming the override.
- An optional sibling `name.dmg.png` (question 3) overrides the derived version. It must be the same size as the color image (`dmg_override_size` error).
- A derived sheet that comes out with 4 opaque shades is a dmg_palette error, with the override as the remedy.
- A .dmg.png in a build without --gbc is an error naming --gbc (question 9).
- A .dmg.png beside indexed art is an error: its shades already are the DMG version.

criteria.label: derived shades match the nearest-shade rule (test)
an override wins over the derived version, and a size mismatch is an error (tests)
two colors in one tile that share a shade warn, naming the tile; across tiles they don't (tests)

data.title: Joint conversion: per-target tiles behind one map and frame list
data.description:
Why: separate tile data per target keeps Ben's shade ruling inside tiles; a shared map keeps the program simple (plan question 1). What:
- Deduplicate tiles on (DMG tile, GBC tile) pairs, with no flips (the DMG has no BG flip), into one tilemap or frame list.
- Make the GBC tiles with `rgbgfx -c <packed palettes>` in gbcli's slot order, plus an attribute map (palette in bits 0-2).
- The agreement check (crates/build/src/images/agree.rs) compares pixel colors, never palette numbers: rgbgfx may choose another palette that fits (research §3).
- The limits bg_tiles_map, vram_tiles and obj_tiles count joint tiles.
- Tiles-only images (assets/tiles/) are deduplicated the same way, with no map; their source tile -> index map is the result.
- Results fill the protocol types from leaf types.

criteria.label: rebuilding both versions from the generated data reproduces both PNGs pixel for pixel (test)
a tile identical in gray but different in color is kept twice (test)
the agreement check fails a GBC conversion that disagrees with the plan (test)

data.title: Dual-mode starter: detect GBC, load palettes and the attribute map
data.description:
What: the starter (crates/build/templates/main.asm) does the following.
- It saves `a == BOOTUP_A_CGB` to an HRAM flag at Start, before `ldh a,[rLY]` overwrites A (lines 19-30).
- On a GBC, with the LCD off, it loads the BG and OBJ palettes through BCPS/BCPD and OCPS/OCPD with autoincrement.
- It writes the attribute map with VBK=1, then sets VBK back to 0.
- It copies the GBC tiles.

The DMG path must not touch VBK. A DMG has no VBK, so the attribute writes would overwrite the tilemap. Decide whether `new --gbc` or `build --gbc` brings the color path into the starter, and say which in the report.

criteria.label: one ROM in two sessions (--model dmg, --model gbc) gives the expected shot in each (goldens)
run --raster on the DMG session shows no VBK, BCPS or attribute-map writes (test)

data.note: Ben approved revision 2 on 2026-11-07 (Q4: one named palette per indexed image; Q5 and the rest: the recommendations; option C parked in backlog.md). Plan imported as Stage 10 under 9b5RBA.

data.text:
Fixed all three (worktree agent-aa1f8fbf7107e325f, uncommitted).
1. Mapper: SameBoy loads the unpadded image (mapper chosen as on mask ROM), then shim gbcli_set_rom_size grows the buffer to the chip ($FF) without GB_configure_cart. ROM-only on a board reaches 32 KiB (no bank register; hardware has 15 CPU address lines). MMM01 on a board refused; non-power-of-two chip size refused. No SameBoy patch.
2. Masks from datasheets: AAA boards/29dl163bd/am29lv160db $FFF (S29AL016D Table 10.1 n5, MX29LV160 PM0866 Table 5 n3, Am29DL16xD 21533 Table 14 n5), 555 boards $7FF (wiring inferred), mx29lv320et $FFF (inferred: PM1575 has no don't-care note), SST39SF040 $7FFF (DS20005022F Table 4-2 n1). Am29LV160D pub 22358 itself unreachable. Parity probe now passes.
3. FlashChip::load split into check_load/finish_load; SameBoy::load finishes the chip only after SameBoy accepts. No rollback.
Docs: project/2026-11-07-flash-model.md "Review fixes"; design §6 correction.

Built (worktree agent-aef9406a4e217d259, uncommitted). `gbcli build --gbc` -> wire `"target":"gbc"` in BuildArgs (typed enum `BuildTarget { Dmg, Gbc }` in crates/protocol/src/toolchain.rs, left off the wire when dmg so old request lines are unchanged). rgbfix gets `-c` for Gbc (project.rs), the failure remedy's "again" command carries `--gbc`, and `BuildMade.target` is always serialized (`"target":"dmg"` now appears in every build result, and the `build` row gains `target=`): the rgbds.txt golden changed for that reason only. Help: `gbcli help rgbds` maps GBC to Pan Docs' CGB and rgbfix -c/-C; the help golden now pins `help rgbds` and `build --help`. Schema lists `target?: "dmg"|"gbc"`.
Tests: build.rs (header $80 vs $00, checksum, result target; failed GBC build's remedy says --gbc), toolchain.rs serde test, topics.rs needle test, rgbds.rs CLI==serve for --gbc and the golden.

Differential test landed in the worktree (uncommitted): crates/engine/tests/opcode_rgbasm_differential.rs, generator crates/engine/tests/rgbasm/grammar.rs, shared rgbasm batch crates/engine/tests/rgbasm/mod.rs (spellings and probes now use it; their per-line helpers are gone).

Batch shape: one main.asm INCLUDEs l<i>.asm per line, each in a 4-byte slot at a fixed ROM0 address (Top: label, line, REDEF LEN EQU @-Top, ds 3-LEN, db LEN, PURGE Top). Own file per line isolates unterminated strings/block comments/trailing backslash; rgbasm names the included file in every diagnostic. rgbasm makes no object if anything fails, so rerun without the failing lines until it links: 2 rgbasm + 1 rgblink per batch of up to 4096 lines. rgbasm takes one input file, so "one file per line in a single invocation" means INCLUDE.

Found and fixed (CASES rows red first): LOW(bc) taken as condition c; ++ read as two pluses (it's string concat); mnemonic ended only at whitespace (rl[hl], set!$6,e); graphics constants >8 pixels refused (rgbasm warns); ldi/ldd refused HIGH(af); negated conditions (!nz) refused; `.` refused as a symbol; rgbasm folds x&&0, x||nonzero, x&0 to constants (bit wBar && 0, a assembles).

Set aside by rgbasm's own error (documented, counted per sweep): undefined symbol/section, jr out of reach, symbol in ldh address out of range, wrong-kind function argument (BANK(-Top)), interpolation, trailing backslash (line continuation), mnemonic alone listing forms.

Timing (load avg 6-10): warm 400 lines 0.20 s; pre-release 40,000 lines (10 seeds) 5.8 s. Exploratory 120k sweeps (seeds 100-129, 200-229) clean after fixes. Red demo: disabling the glued &/% number-prefix rule fails the warm test with 2 lines.

Built (uncommitted, worktree agent-aef9406a4e217d259). The seam LoadHigh imports:
- crates/protocol/src/palettes.rs (new): `Rgb555` newtype (the BCPD/OCPD word; JSON is the integer 0-32767, bit 15 refused; `from_rgb888` keeps each channel's top 5 bits as rgbgfx and census::key do, so a palette entry and a pixel of one #rrggbb are one color; `to_rgb888` is SameBoy's (x<<3)|(x>>2) for previews), `GbcPalette([Rgb555; 4])` (transparent), `NamedPalette { name, colors }`, `NamedPalettes { dmg: Option<GbcPalette>, palettes: Vec<NamedPalette> (file order = index), assignments: BTreeMap<image path under assets/, name> }` with deny_unknown_fields. `dmg` is a typed field, not a palette named "dmg": it's not a GBC palette and can't be assigned.
- crates/protocol/src/images.rs: `ImageKind::Tiles` ("tiles"); `ImageLimit::{GbcPalettes, GbcTileColors, DmgOverrideSize}`; `ImageAsset.tile_indices: Vec<Option<u32>>` (per 8x8 tile / 8x16 unit, row-major; null = transparent unit; target-independent, since tiles dedup on the (DMG, GBC) pair) and `ImageAsset.gbc: Option<GbcImage>`; `GbcImage { art: ImageArt (flattened: "art":"color" | "art":"indexed","palette":NAME), palettes: Vec<GbcPalette> (bg/tileset slot order; empty for sheets), tile_palettes: Vec<Option<u8>> parallel to tile_indices }`; `ImagesMade.gbc: Option<GbcImagesMade { obj_palettes }>`. All new fields skip when empty, so DMG JSON is unchanged: a new CLI golden `crates/gbcli/tests/cli/golden/images.json.txt` (blessed before the type change) pins a whole DMG build line.
- Target per image is implicit: every image has a DMG version; `gbc` is present exactly when the target is GBC. No per-image target list.
- `gbcli schema` lists the types with two examples a test parses into them.
- `ImageKind::Tiles` arms in crates/build are `unreachable!` (find never yields a tileset until the joint leaf).
Not in the types (left to later leaves): whether color art's DMG version was derived or came from name.dmg.png; the named palettes echoed in ImagesMade (the api leaf needs them for PaletteForest labels; decide there whether ImagesMade carries a NamedPalettes).
